key_insight: A lightweight transfer-learning and loss-optimization upgrade to BiSeNetV2 substantially improves seam segmentation robustness under reflective welding conditions without increasing model complexity.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical real-time perception upgrade for construction welding robots that must detect thin seams on shiny metal surfaces with unreliable illumination.
method: Fine-tuned a BiSeNetV2 backbone with transfer learning for seam segmentation.
Replaced the baseline objective with a hybrid Cross-Entropy + Lovász loss to stabilize learning.
Kept the network footprint unchanged while targeting reflection-robust performance.
evidence_signal: The proposed method achieved 81.76% Joint IoU and 90.73% mIoU, improving Joint IoU by 22.36 points over the OHEM baseline while preserving FLOPs, parameters, and inference speed.
watch_item: Reported gains are strongest in reflective construction-welding scenarios, so robustness should still be validated on broader seam types, camera setups, and deployment conditions.
paper_title: Enhanced Seam Segmentation for Automated Welding Robot in Construction Through Transfer Learning: Addressing Limitations of Bilateral Segmentation Network
